newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: EU stands by PLO Jerusalem visit - Irish minister.
newsitem.headline: EU stands by PLO Jerusalem visit - Irish minister.

text.p: European Union President Ireland expressed determination on Saturday to visit the PLO in disputed East Jerusalem, setting the bloc on a potential collision course with Israel's new rightwing government.

Irish Foreign Minister Dick Spring told reporters during an informal EU foreign ministers's session that an EU "troika" of Ireland, the Netherlands and Italy stood by an earlier decision to see the PLO in Orient House, East Jerusalem.
"I certainly feel that we should stick by that decision," said Spring, whose country currently holds the rotating EU presidency.
"We want to make a contribution to the Middle East peace process and it is important that we keep a balance in our relations with the Israeli government and the Palestinian authority," he added.
The topic was due to be discussed by the 15 Foreign Ministers over lunch and a statement was expected when the talks end on Sunday, EU officials said.
Israeli Foreign Minister David Levyy told Spring in Dublin on Thursday that Israel would frown on any plan by the troika to take its fact-finding Middle East mission to East Jerusalem.
Levy said that Palestine Liberation Organisation chairman Yasser Arafat had agreed that the PLO would not hold political meetings in Jerusalem, a city sacred to both Moslems, Jews and Christians.
Irish officials said they would be seeking clarification from the PLO about whether or not they had reached such an agrement with the new Israeli government of Benjamin Netanyahu.

According to Levy, Arafat has agreed to close all PLO political institutions in East Jerusalem and transfer them to places under the control of the newborn Palestinian authority based on the Gaza Strip.
"We'll certainly be seeking clarification on this," said one Irish official. "If it's not Orient House, then there's no point in going," he said.
The EU agreed to go to Orient House at a meeting in July and had not been advised of any change in the location of the PLO's Orient House office, Irish officials said.

No date for the troika visit has been planned but ministers had hoped it might take place before the year's end to review a peace process they fear might be slowed by the killing of Israeli Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin and Netanyahu's election.

They said they had been somewhat reassured by talks between Arafat and Netanyahu this week and hoped that the Middle East peace process was getting back on track but wanted to find out for themselves and maintain its momentum.
Spring outraged the Israeli government last year by visiting Orient House. The Israeli president abruptly cancelled planned talks with Spring in retaliation.
The Israeli government views visit to Orient House as supporting PLO demands to make East Jerusalem the capital of a future Palestinian state.
The city's fate is supposed to be negotiated as part of the Middle East peace process but the Israeli government says it is the unified capital of Israel and will remain as such.
